messages:
deploy-bot: config-only deploy started for prod at 2026-03-20T01:31:30Z. Change set: routing weight tweaks, request timeout increase (2s->3s), batching window shortened (30ms->20ms), and new per-tenant rate caps. Link: https://deploys.internal/release/1934567890 :shipit:
erin_release: quick summary — this is non-code; we're only changing runtime configs. No model artifacts, no infra changes. Rolling out 10%->50% in 15m steps, then 100% if telemetry looks good. Please watch latency and error rates closely. :eyes:
matt_runtime: noted. main concerns: routing weight change could increase tail latency for small-seq requests if batching window reduced. I'll watch P90/P99 for short and long sequences. I'll also pre-warm a couple of dedicated hosts in case of spillover.
sam_oncall: @matt_runtime I'm on standby for the 10% step. If we see error spikes >0.5% for 5m, is the rollback immediate or staged?
matt_runtime: rollback plan: revert config flag to previous snapshot (cmd below) and pin traffic to routing-v1 for 30m while we investigate. Immediate rollback if errors >0.8% sustained for 3m. Staged rollback if 0.5-0.8% — drop to 5% then stop.
```
# rollback command
redwood deploy-config --env prod --snapshot 1934500000 --reason "rollback routing/batch tweak"
```
amy_pm: FYI — customer-impacting thresholds: if latency >500ms for generation median or >1.2s P95 for 3m, escalate to SEV-1 and page oncall. We've queued a few canary prompts (e2e) under CI harness.
julio_qa: running regressions now against the canary prompts. Noted the new timeout, will check for truncated responses and timeouts. Reporting back in ~10m. :mag:
ci-bot: canary test results (initial): 10% cohort — latency median +8ms, P95 +45ms, errors 0.12%. All checks green. Full logs: https://ci.internal/canaries/1934567890
erin_release: good initial signal. Next step at +15m we'll go to 50% if no noisy signals. Also note we added a soft rate cap per-tenant (burst 30r/s, sustained 10r/s) to limit noisy tenants during ramp. Please shout if you see enforcement logs unexpectedly triggering.
sam_oncall: observed a burst of enforcement hits from tenant-id t-405 around +7m, but CI look fine. Matt — does that map to routing shift?
matt_runtime: yes, likely. I patched the transient qps shard mapping; creating temporary bypass rule for t-405 for the 50% step. Command: ``redwood routing update --tenant t-405 --weight 0.0 --reason temp-bypass`` — will re-add weight after observation.
erin_release: decision: proceed to 50% at +15m with t-405 bypassed. Julio keep an eye on truncated responses. If CI or SLOs degrade we rollback to snapshot. :+1: 
deploy-bot: rollout progressed: 10% -> 50% at 1934567940. Monitoring window started.
julio_qa: after 4m at 50% — a few truncated responses from canary set (5 failures/500 requests) attributed to timeout bump? They appear concentrated on long-stream prompts.
matt_runtime: looks like increased timeout caused some batching behavior edge-case for streaming long responses. I'll temporarily revert the timeout for streaming route to 2s, keep non-stream at 3s. Patch command below.
```
redwood config set --env prod --route streaming --timeout 2000
```
erin_release: do it. We'll keep non-stream at 3s for safety. Re-evaluate after 10m.
sam_oncall: monitoring — holding pattern for 10m. If truncated rate drops below 0.3% continue to 100%, otherwise rollback.
ci-bot: updated canary results: truncated failures down to 1/500 after streaming timeout revert. Metrics UI: https://metrics.internal/dashboards/1934567890
erin_release: escalation not needed. proceeding to 100% in 10m if stable. Thanks team. :tada:
deploy-bot: rollout completed to 100% at 1934568050. No rollback executed. Release notes autogenerated: "Config-only: routing weight adjustments, streaming timeout reverted to 2s, general timeout 3s, batching window 20ms, per-tenant soft rate caps." Link: https://releases.internal/1934567890
